id_and_class.theory_title: Avicenna’s Flying Man and Self-Present Soul
id_and_class.summary: Avicenna holds that the human soul is an immaterial, self-subsisting substance whose existence is identical with its awareness of itself. This primitive self-awareness needs no sensation, no bodily awareness, and no reflective act, and his Flying Man thought experiment isolates it by subtracting all sensory input. Sensory experience, by contrast, runs through bodily faculties seated in the brain.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Soul’s Primitive Self-Presence

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: The most basic consciousness is the rational soul’s non-inferential awareness of itself, which Avicenna treats as identical with the soul’s very existence rather than as one of its activities.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Sensation, imagination, estimation, memory, and emotion operate through bodily organs, chiefly the brain. Intellect and fundamental self-awareness belong to an incorporeal rational soul that comes into existence with a suitably organized body and does not perish when the body dies.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (self-awareness belongs intrinsically to an immaterial soul and is not built from bodily processes)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjectivity is the soul’s constant, objectless self-presence, which Avicenna places prior to any act directed at the self. Intentionality runs through the faculties: estimation (wahm) grasps non-sensory meanings in things, as when a sheep apprehends a wolf as dangerous.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Avicenna does not pose a problem of qualia. Qualitative perceptual content belongs to corporeal faculties that receive and combine sensible forms, and he offers no explanation of why sensory processing feels like anything.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: An individual immaterial rational soul; a living organic body; external senses; five internal senses located in the brain’s ventricles; universal, indivisible intelligibles.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Self-awareness is known immediately and non-inferentially, and the Flying Man thought experiment points to it by imaginative subtraction of all sensory and bodily content. Perceptual faculties are studied through Aristotelian faculty psychology and medieval physiology.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Two tiers. Below, five external senses feed five internal senses (common sense, retentive imagination, compositive imagination, estimation, memory). Above, the rational soul holds intellect, reflective self-awareness (intermittent), and primitive self-awareness (continuous).

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Self-awareness (primitive and reflective); Phenomenal (perceptual integration, affective meaning); Memory; Intellect
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Self-presence identical with the soul’s existence. Because primitive self-awareness is the soul’s being rather than an act, it requires no object and no second-order representation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: The soul begins to exist together with its body and is individuated at that moment. Primitive self-awareness then never lapses, persisting through sleep, drunkenness, and total absorption, while reflective self-awareness comes and goes.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Sensory and imaginative processing sits in the brain’s ventricles. The rational soul and its self-awareness have no bodily location.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Bodily faculties build a unified, retained, and meaningful perceptual world that guides behavior. The soul’s intellect grasps universals, a task Avicenna argues no divisible organ can perform.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: The common sense (al-ḥiss al-mushtarak) unifies the sensory modalities into one presentation. Avicenna also argues from the unity of experience that the single subject to which sight, hearing, and thought are all referred cannot be any one faculty among them.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: External senses receive sensible forms, imagination stores and recombines them, estimation extracts non-sensory intentions, and memory retains those intentions. Primitive self-awareness is non-representational.
core_claims_and_evidence: A person created mature, floating in a void with no sensation or memory, would still affirm his own existence while affirming nothing about his body.
Primitive self-awareness is non-propositional, non-inferential, and continuous, and it persists even in sleep and total absorption.
Reflection models of self-awareness fail because any second-order act presupposes the first-personality it was meant to explain.
The intellect receives indivisible universal intelligibles, which cannot be imprinted in a divisible bodily organ, so the rational soul is immaterial.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and phenomenological: thought experiment, argument from the indivisibility of intelligibles, argument from the unity of experience, and Aristotelian faculty psychology.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Scholars disagree on what the Flying Man proves: a demonstration of the soul’s immateriality, a pointer to something already given, or only that self-awareness cannot be constituted by anything bodily. Later Islamic critics pressed hardest on the split between embodied perceptual content and the immaterial subject. Suhrawardī kept immediate self-awareness but rejected the inference to a substantial self, and Aquinas rejected continuous primitive self-awareness, holding that the intellect knows itself through its acts.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The account says nothing about why perception has qualitative character, and its ventricular neuroscience is obsolete. The permanent self-awareness it posits rests on a nonphysical substance that by construction escapes both empirical and introspective check.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a substance dualism framed in Aristotelian vocabulary, though it departs from Aristotle’s view of soul as the form of the body. The open question is how the corporeal faculties and the incorporeal subject join into one experiencer.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since fundamental self-awareness belongs to an immaterial rational soul, an artificial system could at most reproduce the bodily faculties, not the subject of experience.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Avicenna holds that each rational soul, once generated, does not perish when the body dies.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: An immortal, intellect-bearing soul places human consciousness within a larger metaphysical order that outlasts bodily life.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Copying bodily processes would not transfer the immaterial soul, so a digital replica would not continue the self.
